issue.title: Improve recovery and diagnostics for interrupted merge trains

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: Foundational definitions, shared APIs, or supporting layers

issue.body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: merge-train-claim-recovery-20260918 -->
Follow up the non-blocking operational notes in
[review5243821755](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/pull/507#pullrequestreview-5243821755)
of PR #507, as requested in the owner-delegated meta handoff. This does not
block the authorized merge-train contract or reopen its accepted residual
advertisement-to-commit window.

The review identified two limitations. A killed train can leave its shared
member claims held indefinitely, requiring operator recovery. Also, the
post-push violation record reads the claim list while the train owns each
claim, so it records that train's claim rather than identifying an outside
writer that violated the contract.

Required follow-up:

- Provide an explicit recovery procedure or command for interrupted train
  claims, with durable train identity and evidence of termination. Recovery
  must not release claims belonging to a live train or a different owner.
  Do not introduce unconditional expiry of active claims.
- Make violation diagnostics distinguish the verified member SHA, observed
  SHA, the train that held the claim, and any actual writer evidence. When
  the writer is unknown, report that limitation rather than attributing the
  movement to the train merely because its claim is present.
- Add focused fixtures covering interrupted ownership, recovery refusal
  for active or unrelated claims, and truthful moved-member diagnostics.

Preserve the existing whole-transport claims, leased atomic push and
post-push member verification. No server-side member predicate is required.
The claim registry itself is delivered by #579 under #576; this issue
concerns recovery and diagnostics after that implementation.

scope: Nonblocking claim recovery and truthful movement diagnostics; independent issue, not a502 subissue
